Send to Saved Messages after every save

Every change this app makes to settings.toml, other than a sync restore or undo, is queued for Saved Messages five seconds after the last one, so a run of taps is one document. A file imported from Saved Messages is never sent back, and unchanged files are not automatically sent again after delivery. It sends only if the first account is selected when those five seconds end; otherwise that save is not sent.

A peek temporarily shares your Last Seen with %1$s only, so you can read theirs once. Your privacy settings will then be restored exactly as they were. Nobody is notified. If they hide their Last Seen for another reason, nothing will be read.\n\nThis app never makes your last seen visible to everybody on one tap. If that is what you want, use Settings \u2192 Privacy and Security \u2192 Last Seen.
Say why a last seen is hidden

A last seen the server coarsened because of YOUR privacy settings is marked in the chat header and the profile. Nothing is said about one the other person hid, and nothing at all about \"a long time ago\" - the server does not say whether that is inactivity or a block, and this app does not guess.\n\nWhen Last Seen Peeks are allowed, tapping that mark temporarily shares your last seen with only that person, reads theirs, and restores your settings.
What each Last Seen Peek read, and when. A read is forgotten once it is older than trade_remember.

Records which chat is in front of you and for how long, in an append-only screentime.log next to settings.toml. Raw events and nothing else, so changing action_span, active_gap or idle_after in [screen_time] re-reads the history you already have rather than only shaping what happens next. The file never leaves this phone and nothing here is ever sent anywhere.
No chat was open in this period.
Longest first. The bar is the share of the longest chat; the solid part of it is active time. Tap a chat for its own days and hours.
Every day in the period folded onto one clock, so a schedule window can be placed where the time actually goes.
Time spent in chats the running preset was hiding, reached by peeking. Part of the total above, not on top of it.

How often a peek was started in this period, and how long the peeks ran for. Peek is the way out of the preset, so this is how much of the period the preset was not being kept to - which is not the same as the line above it, since most peeks are a look at the chat list itself rather than at any chat in it.
Rows are Monday to Sunday. Darker is more time. Drawn from the whole period, whatever the chips above are filtering.
No budget is set. Add one, or write [[screen_time.budgets]] in settings.toml by hand - either way the file keeps its comments and its layout.

Tap a budget to change it or take it away. What is spent against each one is today\'s, derived from the log like everything else; the same blocks can be written by hand in settings.toml, and editing one here rewrites only the keys you changed.

Sync is manual in this version. Check Saved Messages reads this account\'s Saved Messages and shows what to do next. Nothing changes on this device without your review, and nothing is sent without a fresh check and your confirmation. Settings that sync replaces are kept in History. The settings file may contain chat IDs and names. Saved Messages is a Telegram cloud chat, not end-to-end encrypted, and every signed-in session can read it. state.toml stays local.
